## The question
Student's grades often act as a filter for further opportunity, whether it be further schooling, scholarships, or job opportunities. By understanding what best predicts academic success teachers, parents, and students can best set themselves up for success both during their education and afterward. Using data collected from two different Portuguese schools, we intend to find out which predictors in the dataset are the best at predicting final grades in secondary education in Portuguese schools.  
We would also like to investigate specific relationships, such as that between student’s relationships (familial and friends) and their final grade in math. The intended audience is both educators and students in secondary Portuguese education. 

We found our data on the UCI Machine Learning Library. There are 395 columns and 33 columns seen in the data set, representing 395 individual students from two Portuguese high schools. There are 33 features recorded for each student, recording grades, demographic, school, and social information. This data was collected using school reports and questionnaires. For this project, we will be using final grade in mathematics as the response, which is a numeric variable from 0 to 20. There are many candidate predictors as detailed below. We are specifically interested in the number of absences, age, quality of family relationships and time spent going out with friends. Because this data numerically describes the quality of student’s relationships, it should be able to help answer our question of how those relationships relate to their final grade in math. The data is limited because all of the numeric variables are integers, and many of them are actually categorical.
